glosses: vergoeden, compenseren, goedmaken, terugbetalen
To do (something good) after (something bad) happens.
To pay or reward someone in exchange for work done or some other consideration.

examples.text: It is hard work, but they will compensate you well for it.

glosses: To make up for; to do something in place of something else; to correct, satisfy; to reach an agreement such that the scales are literally or (metaphorically) balanced; to equalize or make even.

examples.text: His loud voice cannot compensate for a lack of personality.
To compensate me for his tree landing on my shed, my neighbor paved my driveway.
The length of the night and the dews thereof do compensate the heat of the day.

, Preface
The pleasures of life do not compensate the miseries.

glosses: To adjust or adapt to a change, often a harm or deprivation.

examples.text: I don't like driving that old car because it always steers a little to the left so I'm forever compensating for that when I drive it. Trust me, it gets annoying real fast.
To compensate for his broken leg, Gary uses crutches.

glosses: To return, restore (a thing to its original owner or location etc.).

examples.text: Give me back my book!

glosses: To contribute money, goods, or, especially, services for charitable purposes, as if in return for one's own success.

examples.text: We organize this Thanksgiving dinner at the old-age home to give back to the community.

glosses: To recede; to retreat.

examples.text: Yet the Fiends ſeemed to come nearer and nearer, but when they were come even almoſt at him, he cried out with a moſt vehement voice, I will walk in the ſtrength of the Lord God; ſo they gave back, and came no farther.

glosses: To exchange two things, with both parties giving one thing and taking another thing.

examples.text: The USTR isn't reciprocating actual tariffs. It's just placing the biggest tariffs on the countries running the biggest trade surpluses.

glosses: To give something else in response (where the \"thing\" may also be abstract, a feeling or action) To make a reciprocal gift.

examples.text: I gave them apples from my tree; they reciprocated with a pie and some apple jelly.
Nugget appreciates the generosity! Nugget will reciprocate with a Monstermon card!

glosses: To move backwards and forwards, like a piston.

examples.text: a reciprocating engine
One brawny smith the puffing bellows plies, / And draws and blows reciprocating air.

glosses: To counter, retort or retaliate.

examples.text: I finally repaid my student loans, just before sending my kids to college.
I'll repay this wrong asap.

On the results of the Kent Coast electrification, which is known to be repaying so far a satisfactory return on the investment in it, a Waterloo-Bournemouth scheme shows reasonable financial promise.

glosses: To make worthwhile; to yield a result worth the effort; to pay off.

examples.text: The possible importance of excessive androgen secretion and the ingestion of agents such as the fluorenamines may repay further investigation.

glosses: To give in return; requite.

examples.text: Although the birds fly north for the summer, they return here in winter.

glosses: To go back in thought, narration, or argument.

examples.text: To return to my story[…]

glosses: To recur; to come again.

examples.text: Winter returns every year.

examples.text: Whan Kyng Marke harde hym sey that worde, he returned his horse and abode by hym.

glosses: To place or put back something where it had been.

examples.text: Please return your hands to your lap.

glosses: To give something back to its original holder or owner.

examples.text: You should return the library book within one month.

glosses: To give in requital or recompense; to requite.

examples.text: Yeah, it's $600,000 but, if it doesn't work, you can always return it. As long as it's undamaged and in the original packaging, I'll give you a full refund.

glosses: To bat the ball back over the net in response to a serve.

examples.text: The player couldn't return the serve because it was so fast.

glosses: To play a card as a result of another player's lead.

examples.text: If one players plays a trump, the others must return a trump.

glosses: To throw a ball back to the wicket-keeper (or a fielder at that position) from somewhere in the field.

examples.text: A facade of sixty feet east and west has a return of twenty feet north and south.

glosses: Something of value given in return for an act.

examples.text: For catching the thief, you'll get a nice reward.
